problem: RL-based object-goal navigation agents perceive too little environmental context from a single view, giving poor visual representations. In complex or confined spaces they also stop exploring novel states and get stuck in deadlocks.
motivation: Object-goal navigation must rely on visual observations alone, so richer spatial context and sustained exploration are both needed. Highly correlated consecutive states within an episode trap the agent in loops, and this drives the paper's constraint on state correlation.
key_idea: Extend the input to five views processed by a Multi-View Visual Transformer for richer spatial context, and constrain the correlation of highly related states within an episode during policy learning to escape deadlocks and encourage novel-state exploration.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract implies that multi-view context improves representation and that the state-correlation constraint drives exploration. It claims the largest gain is in SPL (+16.5%), which suggests the constraint mainly improves path efficiency by avoiding deadlocks.
method: Multi-view visual observation representation: expands the input image perspective to five views so the agent learns spatial context relationships of the environment.
Multi-View Visual Transformer (MVVT): a transformer-based navigation model that fuses the multi-view features into content-rich features for policy learning.
Episode state constraint-based policy learning: constrains the correlation of highly related states within an episode to help the agent escape deadlock and explore novel states.
